# D1 — PVC for `$HOME`: StatefulSet vs Deployment+PVC

Single-replica, long-lived Pod where `$HOME` must survive Pod restart.
Sources in [`../citations.md`](../citations.md).

## Controllers compared

### StatefulSet (with `volumeClaimTemplates`)

- Each Pod gets its own PVC, named `{volumeClaimTemplate.metadata.name}-{pod-ordinal}` [1].
- PVCs persist on Pod restart and Pod reschedule; the Pod's stable ordinal
  identity re-binds the same PVC to the new Pod instance [1].
- Stable identity guarantees apply at N=1 as well as N>1 [1].

### Deployment + explicit PVC

- All Pod replicas reference the same PVC.
- For a `ReadWriteOnce` PVC (Longhorn default access mode), scaling >1
  replicas typically fails — the second replica cannot attach the volume
  if it schedules on another node. For N=1 this is moot.
- No ordinal naming; the Pod is fungible. The PVC name is whatever the
  author chose.

## PVC lifecycle by event

| Event | StatefulSet (defaults) | Deployment+PVC |
|---|---|---|
| Pod delete / restart | PVC retained, same PV re-attached [1] | PVC retained |
| Scale to 0 (then back to N) | PVCs retained, re-attached on scale-up [1][2] | N/A |
| Controller delete | PVCs retained (default); Pods terminated [1][4] | Depends on owner refs — typically retained because PVC has no owner ref to the Deployment |
| `kubectl delete pvc` while Pod uses it | PVC removal postponed until Pod stops (Storage Object in Use Protection) [3] | Same [3] |

> "Deleting and/or scaling a StatefulSet down will _not_ delete the volumes
> associated with the StatefulSet. This is done to ensure data safety,
> which is generally more valuable than an automatic purge of all related
> StatefulSet resources." [1]

> "Deleting the Pods in a StatefulSet will not delete the associated
> volumes. This is to ensure that you have the chance to copy data off
> the volume before deleting it." [4]

## `persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy`

Added alpha 1.23, graduated **beta in 1.27** [2]. Two fields, each accepting
`Retain` (default) or `Delete`:

- `whenDeleted` — applied on StatefulSet deletion
- `whenScaled` — applied on scale-down (Pod removal due to replica
  reduction)

Default for both is `Retain`, matching legacy behavior. With both set to
`Delete`, PVCs are removed when their replica is no longer needed —
explicitly NOT on Pod-level restart [2].

### Known bug (relevant if PSA hardening is in play)

k/k issue #126919: with the `OwnerReferencesPermissionEnforcement` admission
plugin enabled, `whenScaled: Delete` silently fails because the StatefulSet
controller cannot set `blockOwnerDeletion` on the PVC's ownerReference [12].
Closed via PR #126920; verify the fix is in your k3s release before
relying on `whenScaled: Delete`.

## Reclaim policy interaction

Default reclaim policy for dynamically provisioned PVs is inherited from
the StorageClass [3]. With Longhorn's default StorageClass at `Delete`
reclaim, deleting the PVC removes the PV and the underlying Longhorn
volume [3]. Therefore: `persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy.whenDeleted:
Delete` + StorageClass `reclaimPolicy: Delete` = StatefulSet delete erases
the data. Suitable only when you have an external backup or accept data
loss on cleanup.

> "Use caution when deleting a PVC, as it may lead to data loss." [4]

## N-instance pattern: one StS per operator vs N replicas in one StS

For "N copies of the same workload, one per operator-user":

- **One StatefulSet with N replicas:** PVCs named `data-<sts>-0` ...
  `data-<sts>-{N-1}`. Adding/removing operators requires scaling, which
  is fine but couples the per-operator PVC's name to ordinal — adding
  user `bob` after `alice` and `carol` requires careful ordinal
  management. Scale-down removes the highest-ordinal Pod, not necessarily
  the operator you intended to deprovision.
- **One StatefulSet per operator:** Each operator gets a separate
  StatefulSet (`home-alice`, `home-bob`), each with its own
  `volumeClaimTemplates`. Adding/removing an operator is a STS-level
  create/delete. PVC names are operator-named. No ordinal coupling.
- **One Deployment per operator + explicit PVC:** Functionally similar
  to the per-operator StatefulSet for N=1. Simpler manifest (no
  `volumeClaimTemplates`). No per-Pod stable network identity, but for
  a sandbox accessed via the cluster Service or ingress that doesn't
  matter.

**Recommended pattern:** one controller per operator. The per-replica
ordinal model in a single shared StatefulSet adds operator-management
friction without benefit at N=1 each. Between per-operator StatefulSet vs
per-operator Deployment, the StatefulSet has marginally better default
behavior because `volumeClaimTemplates` automatically provisions and
binds the PVC, and the per-replica PVC retention story is unambiguous [1][2].

## Counter-perspective: when neither is ideal

- **Longhorn-level data loss is orthogonal to controller choice.**
  Longhorn has documented data-loss failure modes after network partition
  events and "volume stuck deleting" bugs across versions. Choosing
  StatefulSet vs Deployment does not change those risks; a backup
  strategy does.
- **Multi-Attach errors on node failure** affect both patterns equally.
  When a node dies while holding an RWO attachment, the new Pod cannot
  attach until the stale attachment is released (either via Longhorn's
  force-detach setting or manual intervention).
- **An Operator pattern** (a custom controller managing per-tenant
  resources) is the right answer when the per-tenant lifecycle involves
  more than just a PVC and Pod (e.g., per-tenant ConfigMap, Secrets,
  Service, NetworkPolicy). For the project's stated scope — just `$HOME`
  persistence — a CRD/Operator is overkill.

  beta in 1.27 is implied by the kubernetes.io statefulset doc snippet

- No source directly compares "one StatefulSet per tenant vs N replicas"

  from the per-Pod PVC binding behavior and the operator-lifecycle

- Longhorn-specific data-loss issue references in counter-discovery are
